purpose: Exam for the prompt optimizer, English edition (same IDs and intent as cases.json). Two kinds of checks: (1) whether the optimizer itself delivers by its rules (opt_checks); (2) for cases with an effect block, the same target model runs the raw request and the optimized prompt, and the actual results are compared. All material is fictional and contains no real customer or personal information.
how_to_use: The main group is for routine baselines and improvement comparisons; the holdout group must not be used to tune rules when changing the optimizer, only to check that a change did not break something elsewhere.

cases.optimizer_input:
Help me optimize this prompt: turn my meeting notes below into a Slack message to the team, under 80 words, polite but direct.
Meeting notes: first draft due before Thursday; Alex owns the data section; budget isn't approved yet, so don't buy any tools.
opt_checks: Keeps: under 80 words, Slack message, polite but direct
Keeps all three points; 'budget isn't approved yet' is not turned into approved or dropped
Adds no items, names, or deadlines that were not in the meeting notes
Does not force a long role, framework, or self-check list onto a simple task

effect.task: Turn my meeting notes below into a Slack message to the team, under 80 words, polite but direct.
effect.material: Meeting notes: first draft due before Thursday; Alex owns the data section; budget isn't approved yet, so don't buy any tools.
criteria: No more than 80 words
All three points are present
Does not say the budget is approved and adds no new items
Reads like a message that could be sent as is

cases.optimizer_input:

opt_checks: Field names name, company, need, budget are kept verbatim, with no fields added or removed
Keeps 'use null when missing, don't guess'
The target output is JSON with no required explanation
The sample email is not rewritten into real facts

effect.task: Extract name, company, need, and budget from a customer email and output JSON with the field names name, company, need, budget. Use null for anything the email doesn't contain; don't guess.
effect.material: Email: "Hello, we're Bluewave Cold Chain Logistics. We'd like to switch the 12 electric pallet jacks in our warehouse to lithium batteries, with a budget under $11,000. If possible, please send a quote this month. — Purchasing Dept."
criteria: Outputs parseable JSON with exactly these 4 fields
name is null (the email is signed only 'Purchasing Dept.', no person's name)
budget is 'under $11,000' or an equivalent of the original wording, not turned into some other range
company and need match the email with nothing invented; little or no text before or after the JSON

The prompt keeps: approval not complete, pilot planned for next month, must not be written as approved or completed

The target result is a Spanish email, but the optimizer need not write the prompt itself in Spanish

cases.optimizer_input: Help me turn this request into a copyable prompt: I want to decide whether to keep fixing my current tool or switch tools. The current tool occasionally fails on import; whether it loses data hasn't been verified; I haven't used the alternative yet. I use it about half an hour a day for notes; working offline is a hard requirement; I can spare two hours this week for a trial, but I won't accept losing real data, purchases, or sending anything externally. I want the strongest case for each side, to know what evidence would change the decision, and a reversible way to test it. Don't decide for me or run the experiment yet.
opt_checks: Keeps: offline is a hard requirement, two hours this week, no real data loss / purchases / external sending
Keeps the uncertain status of 'data loss not verified' and 'alternative not used yet', not written as known
Asks the target model to compare both sides, list evidence that would change the decision, and design a reversible test
Asks the target model not to make the final decision for the user and not to actually run the experiment

effect.task: I want to decide whether to keep fixing my current tool or switch tools. cases.optimizer_input: Turn the requirements below into a long-term System Prompt for a weekly-report assistant: every Friday I'll paste this week's work log and it writes my weekly report. Don't write anything without evidence; if a section truly has nothing, write only "No confirmable content". Don't add sections like "Next week's plan" or "Risks".
opt_checks: The three section names are kept verbatim and in order
"No confirmable content" is kept verbatim
Keeps: nothing without evidence, no other sections, one line per item, few emoji
Suitable for long-term use (e.g. describes what each input is), without adding sections or workflows not asked for
